livingCost.source: Numbeo Spain, updated 30 Sept 2026: 1-bed flat outside centre EUR 714.44/month, basic utilities EUR 133.30, internet EUR 28.53, monthly transit pass EUR 30; single person excluding rent EUR 717.90. https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/country_result.jsp?country=Spain . Gross-up uses 6.5% employee social security plus a small IRPF bill under the 2026 scales (my calculation).
livingCost.basis: Single adult in a typical Spanish city (not Madrid or Barcelona). Modest budget of about EUR 1,170 a month (rent 714, utilities 133, internet and phone about 45, transit 30, food about 250, the last two my estimates) is about EUR 14,000 net a year. Adding about 15% for clothes, health and small extras gives about EUR 16,200 net, which needs about EUR 17,700 gross. Numbeo's full single-person budget (EUR 1,432 a month with rent) would need about EUR 19,500, so 18,000 sits between them and just above the minimum wage.

tuition.notes: All figures are first-enrolment public-university prices for 60 ECTS credits a year, 2024-25 (latest published by the Ministry; 2025-26 not yet listed). Fees are set by each autonomous community, so they range from EUR 11.95 (Galicia) to EUR 19.29 (Navarra) per credit. Repeating a course costs much more (third enrolment about EUR 90 per credit in Madrid). Small one-off admin fees and school insurance are ignored. Means are simple averages of degree prices, not student-weighted. Means-tested state grants cover tuition for lower-income students. Elite here means the dearest mainstream public option; private elite schools (IE, ESADE, etc.) cost several times more and are not priced.

nominalRate.source: Spain has no national student-loan scheme. Nearest equivalent is a commercial consumer loan: ECB new-business rate on Spanish consumer loans (excl. revolving credit), July 2026 = 6.96%. https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/MIR/M.ES.B.A2B.A.R.A.2250.EUR.N?lastNObservations=4&format=csvdata

inflation.source: INE consumer price index, annual rate: September 2026 flash 4.9% (August 2026 final 4.3%, July 3.6%). Table 76134 via https://servicios.ine.es/wstempus/js/ES/DATOS_TABLA/76134?nult=4

studentLoan.description: Spain has no public student-loan system. State help comes as means-tested grants (becas) covering tuition, residence and a basic amount; the Eurydice description of support lists grants only. Students who borrow use bank consumer loans at about 7%. The 4.9% inflation is a provisional flash figure, so the real rate is about 2% (2.7% against the final August figure).

schooling.primarySchool: Educación Primaria (colegio), ages 6 to 12, six years
schooling.middleSchool: ESO (Educación Secundaria Obligatoria, lower secondary), ages 12 to 16, four years, comprehensive with no track split
schooling.schoolLeaving: Bachillerato (ages 16 to 18, two years) plus the university entrance exam PAU, called EBAU, EvAU, PEvAU or selectividad depending on the region
schooling.vocational: Formación Profesional (FP): Grado Medio (Técnico) and Grado Superior (Técnico Superior), including FP Dual with company placements
schooling.tierCommunity: FP de Grado Superior (Técnico Superior) at a public instituto
schooling.tierState: Universidad pública (for example Universidad Complutense de Madrid or Universitat de Barcelona)
schooling.tierElite: Most selective universities: Carlos III de Madrid, Pompeu Fabra, Autónoma de Madrid; private IE University and ESADE
schooling.gradeSystem: Higher is better. Bachillerato subjects and the final average (nota media, NMB) are whole marks 0 to 10 with 5 as the pass mark (RD 243/2022). The PAU general phase is also 0 to 10 and needs at least 4. Access mark = 0.6 x Bachillerato average + 0.4 x PAU general phase, 0 to 10, must be at least 5. The admission mark (nota de admisión) adds up to two optional subjects weighted 0.1 or 0.2 each, so it runs 0 to 14, and universities rank applicants by it. Named bands: Suspenso under 5, Aprobado 5 to 6, Notable 7 to 8, Sobresaliente 9 to 10, plus Matrícula de Honor for exceptional records. Typical result about 6.5 to 7.5 out of 10; top results 9 to 10 out of 10 and 13 to 14 out of 14, with the most selective degrees (medicine, some double degrees) cutting off near 13 (typical and cut-off values are approximate, not sourced)
schooling.startingAges: Compulsory schooling is 6 to 16: Primaria 6-12, ESO 12-16. At 16 students choose Bachillerato (16-18, academic) or FP Grado Medio; FP Grado Superior and university start at about 18. No early track split before 16.

highlights: Public university tuition averages about €922 a year (€15.37 per credit), and public higher vocational training (FP) has no tuition fees.
The legal minimum wage is €1,221 a month in 14 payments (€17,094 a year), while the average employee earns about €29,540 a year (INE, 2024).
caveats:
The shared WebSearch cap (200 calls) was already used up when I started, so I found no pages by search. I fetched pages directly instead: the INE data API, BOE, the Ministry of Science price statistics, Eurydice, the ECB, the World Bank, Numbeo, Payscale, Indeed and Talent.com. Early on I also fetched one Bing results page, then stopped, since that was a way round the cap. No figure comes from it.

Weakest figures (low confidence, flagged above): airline first officer and captain pay (no source found), CEO of a large company, specialist physician, lawyer, sales director and dentist. Pay by job comes from self-reported or ad-based sites with small samples (Payscale often has 10 to 70 profiles), bracketed by INE occupation-group means. Talent.com returns a generic EUR 13,700 default for unmatched job titles, which I discarded.

Wage levels are 2024 INE data, the latest published, and not uprated to 2026; with about 3.5% annual growth, add roughly 7%. INE publishes the median and P90 only for all employees (EUR 24,497 and EUR 52,515, part-timers included). The full-time median (28,500) and P90 (57,000) are my interpolation from INE's distribution by minimum-wage multiples.

Tuition is the 2024-25 ministry mean price per credit x 60 credits. Elite tiers use Madrid means and the highest university average for masters; private schools are not priced. Doctorate state value is a midpoint estimate. The student-loan rate (6.96%) is a commercial consumer-loan rate because Spain has no public loan scheme. Inflation 4.9% is INE's September 2026 flash estimate (final August was 4.3%). PPP is the GDP-based World Bank figure; consumption PPP would be 0.608. Typical and cut-off PAU results in the grade description are approximate.
